names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 29 mai, «Sfânta Muceniță Teodosia, fecioara».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 29. мај ст. ст., „Света мученица Теодосија Тирска“ — Света is not a rank and мученица is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`; strip the two and „Теодосија Тирска“ is left, the name with the city that distinguishes her. **Тирска IS WHAT KEEPS THREE WOMEN APART AND IT WAS MEASURED.** `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Теодосија Тирска» and `[('theodosia-of-caesarea-in-palestine', 'sr')]` for the bare «Теодосија» — a woman beheaded at the same Caesarea in Palestine, kept by this same book on its own 25 March. **A bare form here would have folded this martyr of 308 onto that martyr of 361 on the strength of a shared city**, and the day’s own third entry is a third Theodosia besides. The Greek rows give this folder no form at all and the Romanian gives «Teodosia», the bare name.

Read out of the title on the name link behind her line for 3 апреля ст. ст., name page 2714, «Мученица Феодосия Тирская, Кесарийская», with the rank word stripped off the front and the second toponymic — the city she died in, not a second woman — left in the life rather than folded into the form. The day’s own line declines the forename and the grade, «Феодосии девы». No folder holds this form or the bare «Феодосия». `theodosia-of-caesarea-in-palestine` is the corpus’s other Theodosia and a different woman — two other books keep her on 25 March beside Pelagia and date her 361 — so the second toponymic here is read as the city of this woman’s death and nothing is moved onto that folder. The name is kept out of the prose for the reciprocal-row rule and set down here instead.

feast.note: The same calendar keeps a feast of her relics on the Julian 29 May and names it outright: its page for that day prints «Мц. Феодосии девы, Тирской (ок. 307-308).» and the reading behind that line is titled «Перенесение мощей мученицы Феодосии Тирской» and says «29 мая празднуется память перенесения ее мощей в Константинополь и Венецию» — the translation of her relics to Constantinople and to Venice (https://days.pravoslavie.ru/Days/20260529.html and https://days.pravoslavie.ru/Life/life1166.htm, read 8 October 2026). One row per church is the schema, so the translation is recorded here and she does not render on it. That day page prints a hymn whose heading carries her own epithet, «Ин кондак преподобномученицы Феодосии девы, Тирской» (глас 4), and it was NOT copied into this folder, the row standing on another day; the heading also gives her the rank «преподобномученицы», which belongs to the other Theodosia the same day keeps, the nun of Constantinople, and the mixture is the calendar's own.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 3 апреля ст. ст. — «Мц. Феодосии девы (307-308).»

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 11.06.2026 (29. мај ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Теодосија Тирска“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, on the same menologion 29/5 the Romanian row already carries; the Greek and Russian rows are `undocumented`. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 29 May is. **TWO DIFFERENT THEODOSIAS ON ONE DAY OF ONE BOOK, AND A THIRD ALREADY IN THE CORPUS.** The day’s second and third entries are both Theodosias, and the Prologue tells them apart by rank and epithet alone — „Света мученица Теодосија Тирска“ against „Преподобна мученица Теодосија“. **The corpus keeps them as two folders and they stay two**: one dies at Caesarea in Palestine under Maximian in 308 and the other at Constantinople under Leo the Isaurian in 730. **And the fold reaches a third woman**: `theodosia-of-caesarea-in-palestine` already holds the bare `sr` form «Теодосија», written in this same wave off the Prologue’s own Julian 25 March, where she is beheaded with Pelagia in 361. **That folder was opened and read before either row here was written**, because her place of death is the same Caesarea in Palestine as the 29 May martyr’s and the bare name is the same string — **and she is a third woman**: a different day of this same book, a different year, a different companion. **Two commemorations on one calendar means two women, and three mean three.** **A FIRST DATE AND A FIRST EMPEROR.** The existing life closes „The page prints no year“, and doxologia dates her only by Eusebius’s „the persecution had run over them for five years“ and the second day of April. The Prologue states a year — „Чесно пострада и прослави се 308. године“ — so `dates.death` is 308 to 308, `basis: "traditional"`. **It also names the emperor, „У време цара Максимијана“, where doxologia names only the governor Urban; the reign is used for nothing and no year was derived from it.** **doxologia’s second of April is a day of death twenty-seven days off the 29 May all the calendars keep her on, and there is no field for a day of death**; it was already in the prose and nothing was moved. **THE SAME SAYING IN THE SAME WORDS, OFF TWO HOSTS IN TWO LANGUAGES.** „Видите ли, колика је слава и благодат Христа мога, које сте ме хтели лишити?“ against doxologia’s *see how great is the glory and the gift of my Christ, of which you wished to deprive me*. **The appearance to her parents the following night, the reproach in it, and the reason for the reproach — that they had held her back from the martyr’s contest — are all in both books.** So are the stone hung at her neck, the drowning in the depth of the sea, the angels bringing her up alive to the shore, her coming again before the judge and the beheading. **New here, and it is little**: that she was **surrounded by many other saved maidens** in the vision, where doxologia has her in the midst of the holy virgins with a golden cross and a crown; and that she **blessed and encouraged the bound Christians for a martyr’s death**, where doxologia has her speak to them of the kingdom of God and ask to be remembered. **What the Prologue has not got**: the governor Urban, the iron claws, the beasts that would not harm her, the dove brighter than gold, and her age. `martyr` and `virgin` are both corroborated — „ова благочестива девица“ — and **no type was added**; the folder already prints *Virgin Martyr Theodosia* from the pair and nothing about it changed. Nobody in the entry gains a row: the parents are unnamed, the judge is a persecutor, and Maximian is an emperor no calendar read here keeps. `related` stays empty. No `locations`, although Caesarea in Palestine and Tyre are both named. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: La fapta bună muceniţă, cu osârdie deprinzându-te, te-ai făcut vas iubit al lui Hristos şi locaş iubit al Preasfântului Duh. Pentru aceasta ai ruşinat pe vrăjmaşul, cel ce se luptă cu neamul omenesc, bine pătimind şi arătat cu sabia credinţei ai ucis pe cel cu nume de fiară, Teodosia; şi bucurându-te te-ai mutat la cer, cerând pururea mare milă, celor ce cu credinţă te cinstesc pe tine.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Mucenițe Teodosia, fecioara

english.text: Training thyself with zeal in the good work, O martyr, thou becamest a beloved vessel of Christ and a beloved dwelling of the All-Holy Spirit. Therefore thou didst shame the enemy who fights against the human race, suffering well; and openly, with the sword of faith, thou didst slay him whose name is the beast's, O Theodosia. Rejoicing, thou wast taken up to heaven, asking always great mercy for those who honour thee with faith.

death.note: The range is the source’s own and is not narrowed. days.pravoslavie.ru closes her line for 3 апреля ст. ст. with «(307-308)», and of the two lives behind it one opens «пострадала в 307 или 308 году» and the other «пострадала в 307 году». The folder held a flat 308 off doxologia and the Ohrid Prologue, both of which keep her on 29 May, the day this book gives to the translation of her relics and not to her death.
